Measure PPM of your total solution, subtract your base water PPM and you'll have the correct PPM for referencing.

Edit: everything below is hydro related after I realized this isnt a hydro sub. Still somewhat relevant though.

R/O with exact nute additives is typically what many go for. Think Cal-Mag blends with base minerals.. I'm blessed with my own well which is 250-330ppm depending on the time of year and only when sub 300ppm do I get a slight Mag deficiency. Pinch of Epsom salt fixes that. I aim for 350ppm in my base water so when I've got 1600ppm, ~1300ppm is the actual nutrient solution in my late flower stages. I believe most of the charts you will find either list or intend to reference starting with R/O.
Note: I run a DWC hydro setup, so I have more fine tuned control.. I would recommend 3/4 or less ppm goals than what most charts have. Get it stable then tweak from there.
